answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a whisper as the anchor of the cost.
